Chỉ chọn NO nếu tác giả phủ định rõ phản ứng ngạc nhiên của các chuyên gia.

questions.prompt: As farmland in the uplands has been given up, the karn has found new ground to occupy.

explanation.step1: As farmland in the uplands has been given up , the karn has found new ground to occupy . Ý câu hỏi: tác giả có nói karn lan sang nơi khác khi việc canh tác ở vùng đồi núi bị bỏ hay không?
explanation.step2: Dựa vào tên loài `karn`, ta tìm đến câu (3) đoạn 8, bắt đầu bằng “Elsewhere the karn has already been resettled”. Sau đó đọc tiếp để kiểm tra mối liên hệ với việc canh tác. Đoạn 8 — Elsewhere the karn has already been resettled
explanation.step3: Đoạn 8: Elsewhere the karn has already been resettled in the Kessel range , the Ombrian Alps, the western Duvray hills and the Astel mountains, and found its own way back into many districts more . Much as the wolf , bear, beaver, boar, bison and elk did earlier , the cat has spread as farming withdrew from the hills and as people grasp that protecting eye-catching wildlife earns more than hunting it, tourists being willing to pay for a sighting . Câu (3): karn đã trở lại nhiều nơi khác . Câu (5): tác giả gọi karn là “the cat” và nói nó lan rộng khi việc canh tác rút khỏi vùng đồi núi .
explanation.step4: Câu hỏi nói: đất canh tác vùng đồi núi bị bỏ (“ farmland in the uplands has been given up ”) và karn có thêm nơi sinh sống (“ has found new ground to occupy ”). Bài đọc nói: karn trở lại nhiều nơi khác (“ found its own way back into many districts more ”); tác giả nói nó lan rộng khi việc canh tác rút khỏi vùng đồi núi (“the cat has spread as farming withdrew from the hills”). Đối chiếu paraphrasing: farmland in the uplands has been given up farming withdrew from the hills has found new ground to occupy has spread + found its own way back into many districts more Đáp án đúng: YES — nhận định phù hợp với điều tác giả nói. Đáp án NO Nếu thấy ngoại lệ “save Varestia” ở cuối đoạn 8, em có thể nghĩ tác giả phủ nhận sự lan rộng Nhưng cụm đó nói về rewilding quy mô lớn tại Varestia, không phủ nhận việc karn đã lan rộng. Chỉ chọn NO nếu tác giả nói karn không lan rộng khi việc canh tác rút khỏi vùng đồi núi. NOT GIVEN Sai vì câu (5) nêu cả việc karn lan rộng lẫn hoàn cảnh việc canh tác rút khỏi vùng đồi núi. Chỉ chọn NOT GIVEN nếu bài không cho biết mối liên hệ đó.

questions.prompt: Varestia has moved as quickly as other parts of the mainland in bringing back its lost predators.

explanation.step1: Varestia has moved as quickly as other parts of the mainland in bringing back its lost predators . Ý câu hỏi: tác giả có cho rằng Varestia đưa các loài thú săn mồi trở lại nhanh ngang những nơi khác trên đất liền không?
explanation.step2: Dựa vào địa danh `Varestia` và ý so sánh với những nơi khác => ta tìm đến câu: `Rewilding on a grand scale is happening almost everywhere, save Varestia.` Đoạn 8
explanation.step3: Đoạn 8: Elsewhere the karn has already been resettled in the Kessel range, the Ombrian Alps , the western Duvray hills and the Astel mountains , and found its own way back into many districts more . Rewilding on a grand scale is happening almost everywhere , save Varestia . Câu (4): karn đã được đưa trở lại ở nơi khác. Câu (8): tái hoang dã quy mô lớn diễn ra gần như khắp nơi, trừ Varestia .
explanation.step4: Câu hỏi nói: Varestia tiến nhanh ngang những nơi khác (“as quickly as other parts of the mainland”). Bài đọc nói: karn đã được đưa trở lại ở nơi khác (“already been resettled”), còn Varestia là ngoại lệ đối với tái hoang dã quy mô lớn (“save Varestia”). Lập trường của tác giả trái với nhận định rằng Varestia đang theo kịp những nơi khác . Đối chiếu paraphrasing: bringing back its lost predators the karn has already been resettled as quickly as other parts of the mainland almost everywhere, save Varestia Đáp án đúng: NO Đáp án YES Sai vì tác giả nêu Varestia là ngoại lệ, không phải nơi đang theo kịp những nơi khác. Chỉ chọn YES nếu tác giả nói Varestia cũng tiến nhanh ngang các nơi đó. NOT GIVEN Có thể phân vân vì bài không đưa số đo tốc độ cụ thể Nhưng tác giả đã thể hiện sự đối lập qua việc karn đã trở lại nơi khác và tái hoang dã quy mô lớn diễn ra gần khắp nơi trừ Varestia. Chỉ chọn NOT GIVEN nếu bài không cho biết Varestia khác các nơi khác về tiến độ này.

questions.prompt: A new organisation has already been set up to drive rewilding across the whole of Varestia.

explanation.step1: A new organisation has already been set up to drive rewilding across the whole of Varestia . Ý câu hỏi: Tác giả có nói tổ chức này đã được thành lập , chứ không chỉ mới được lên kế hoạch, hay không?
explanation.step2: Dựa vào địa danh `Varestia` và ý về một tổ chức thúc đẩy rewilding => ta tìm đến câu (4), đoạn 9, bắt đầu bằng “Plans are afoot for a body”. Đoạn 9 — Plans are afoot for a body
explanation.step3: Đoạn 9: Plans are afoot for a body to spur the rewilding of land and sea throughout Varestia , its ultimate aim being to restore to the country's ecosystems the scarcest species of all: hope .
explanation.step4: Câu hỏi nói: tổ chức đã được thành lập (“has already been set up”). Bài đọc nói: tác giả cho biết đang có kế hoạch về tổ chức đó (“Plans are afoot for a body”). Đây là quan điểm trái với tình trạng đã thành lập trong câu hỏi. Đối chiếu paraphrasing: has already been set up Plans are afoot for a body to drive rewilding to spur the rewilding across the whole of Varestia throughout Varestia Đáp án đúng: NO Đáp án YES Nếu chỉ thấy bài đọc nhắc đến một tổ chức (“a body”), sẽ dễ chọn YES Nhưng tác giả nói tổ chức ấy mới ở bước kế hoạch (“Plans are afoot”). Chỉ chọn YES nếu tác giả nói tổ chức đã được thành lập. NOT GIVEN Nếu tìm đúng cụm “has already been set up” mà không thấy, sẽ dễ chọn NOT GIVEN Nhưng tác giả có cho biết tình trạng của tổ chức qua “Plans are afoot”. Chỉ chọn NOT GIVEN nếu tác giả không cho biết tổ chức đã thành lập hay mới được lên kế hoạch.

passages.title: UK companies need more effective boards of directors
content: [A]  A run of serious governance failures — governance being the way a company is steered at its most senior level — has left firms in Britain, and in other countries too, with good reason to contemplate a drastic rethink of what their directors do. Nobody would pretend that sitting on a board is straightforward these days. When the financial system collapsed in 2008, the downturn that followed proved deeper and longer-lasting than almost anyone had predicted, and the many autopsies of the episode cast blame in every direction. Regulators, central banks, auditors and governments alike found themselves under suspicion. As for the directors and managers of the banks, their much-publicised shortcomings were raked over at length in one report, inquiry and commentary after another.

[B]  One consequence of all this attention is that the running of companies generally has turned into a matter of fierce public argument, and the burden carried by directors has grown heavier along with it. Consider the most basic point of all: the sheer number of hours a directorship now demands has climbed steeply, which throws doubt on the familiar arrangement whereby part-time, independent non-executives oversee a firm. A board that used to gather perhaps eight to ten times a year may now face a schedule in which the occasions calling for its attention and its decisions have multiplied. On top of that, each meeting brings more to read and to prepare. When agendas swell in this way, the room left for genuine debate has to be squeezed so that the day's business can be got through.

[C]  To manage the load, much of a board's work is frequently handed down to committees. That may well be the more efficient route, yet it can leave the full board only loosely engaged with several of the questions that matter most. Indeed, a meeting of the audit committee not infrequently outlasts the gathering of the main board. Procedure ends up standing in for genuine exchange, and true collaboration is the casualty, so that boxes get ticked while the underlying problems are left untackled.

[D]  A bolder answer, suited perhaps to a handful of very large firms whose operations are sprawling and intricate, is the professional board, on which members might serve three or four days a week and enjoy the backing of their own dedicated staff and advisers. A structure of that sort carries obvious dangers, and firm ground rules would be needed to stop it from treading on management's territory by involving itself in the daily conduct of the business. Questions of how to recruit such directors, how to reward them and how to preserve their independence might well surface, and the arrangement would hardly suit every company. Even so, boards that were more professional and far better briefed would have served the banks especially well, for there the salaried executives commanded a depth of inside knowledge their part-time colleagues could never match — a gulf that left those non-executives unable to grasp or foresee the 2008 crash.

[E]  A charge levelled again and again at boards is that too little of their attention goes to the long view — to strategy, to sustainability, to governance — while far too much is fixed on immediate profit. Both the rules they work under and the very shape of the market push them in this direction. The relentless rhythm of quarterly reporting can warp the choices a board reaches, since every four months its directors must 'hit the numbers' to feed a market forever hungry for fresh data. Such pressure rewards one particular breed of investor, the sort who slips in and out of a holding purely for a quick return and never troubles to discuss strategy or performance with the company. The tendency has sharpened as capital has gone global and as automated trading systems have come into ever wider use. Corporate culture bends to fit, and management, by and large, is paid to meet its commercial goals.

[F]  Pay for chief executives has turned into a battlefield on which investors, managers and board members wage set-piece struggles — sometimes out of sight, though more and more often under the bright lights of press coverage. To many observers that openness is precisely what transparency and sound governance demand, since shareholders bring their weight to bear on pay so as to force boards into dismissing chief executives who fail to deliver. Once such votes had been made legally binding, their capacity to strike down a company's pay policies grew stronger still. Chairing the remuneration committee can prove a lonely and badly exposed post, as Margery Thorne discovered at Kestrel Bank: she was obliged to step down after weathering a storm of criticism for defending a huge bonus destined for the chief executive — the irony being that, behind the committee's closed doors, she was widely believed to have argued against it.

[G]  Out of the financial crisis grew a broader conversation about what a company is actually for, together with a sharpened concern for corporate ethics. Faith in the corporation has worn thin, and thinkers such as Adrian Feld — whose bestseller The Limits of the Market has found a wide readership — now press hard questions about the morality of capitalism and of the market economy itself. In every sector, boards will have to broaden their outlook so as to take such matters in, and doing so may mean recasting the very goals a company sets for itself. These are demanding times.

questions.correct: Responsibility for the crisis falling on a wide range of outside institutions

explanation.step1: Đoạn A: A run of serious governance failures — governance being the way a company is steered at its most senior level — has left firms in Britain, and in other countries too, with good reason to contemplate a drastic rethink of what their directors do . Nobody would pretend that sitting on a board is straightforward these days . When the financial system collapsed in 2008 , the downturn that followed proved deeper and longer-lasting than almost anyone had predicted , and the many autopsies of the episode cast blame in every direction . Regulators , central banks, auditors and governments alike found themselves under suspicion . As for the directors and managers of the banks , their much-publicised shortcomings were raked over at length in one report, inquiry and commentary after another . Câu (1)–(2): đặt bối cảnh thất bại quản trị và sự phức tạp của công việc trong hội đồng quản trị. Câu (3)–(4): khủng hoảng dẫn đến việc quy trách nhiệm về nhiều phía ; câu (4) cụ thể hóa bằng các nhóm tổ chức bị nghi ngờ . Câu (5): tiếp tục mạch xem xét trách nhiệm, chuyển sang giám đốc ngân hàng. Đoạn A — cast blame
explanation.step2: Sau khủng hoảng, trách nhiệm bị truy xét rộng khắp , từ các tổ chức bên ngoài đến giám đốc ngân hàng. Đáp án đúng: Responsibility for the crisis falling on a wide range of outside institutions ( Trách nhiệm về cuộc khủng hoảng bị quy cho nhiều tổ chức bên ngoài ). Đối chiếu paraphrasing: Responsibility cast blame a wide range of outside institutions in every direction + Regulators + governments How closer examination has affected firms “ (Tác động của việc xem xét kỹ hơn đối với doanh nghiệp) ”: câu (5) nói các thiếu sót bị soi xét (“raked over”). Nhưng đoạn tập trung vào những bên bị xem xét trách nhiệm, không phải tác động của sự giám sát lên hoạt động doanh nghiệp. A suggestion for running the board differently “ (Một đề xuất thay đổi cách vận hành hội đồng quản trị) ”: câu (1) nhắc đến việc xem xét lại mạnh mẽ (“a drastic rethink”). Nhưng đây mới là lời đặt vấn đề; đoạn chưa đưa ra mô hình hay cách vận hành thay thế. Why every part of a business may have to be rethought “ (Vì sao mọi bộ phận của doanh nghiệp có thể phải được xem xét lại) ”: cùng có ý xem xét lại. Nhưng câu (1) chỉ nói đến công việc của các giám đốc (“what their directors do”), không phải mọi bộ phận của doanh nghiệp.
explanation.step3: Bóc tách cấu trúc câu (S-V-O) và đối chiếu nghĩa.
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: Responsibility for the crisis falling on a wide range of outside institutions

explanation.step1: Đoạn B: One consequence of all this attention is that the running of companies generally has turned into a matter of fierce public argument , and the burden carried by directors has grown heavier along with it . On top of that, each meeting brings more to read and to prepare. Gợi ý: dấu hiệu bổ sung (“On top of that”) cho biết câu này tiếp tục nêu thêm công việc. Gánh nặng tăng đã rõ ở các câu trước nên có thể bỏ phần nội dung phía sau. Câu (5): công việc tăng => thời gian thảo luận bị thu hẹp để giải quyết hết công việc. Đoạn B — On top of that
explanation.step2: Đoạn trình bày tác động của việc bị xem xét kỹ hơn lên doanh nghiệp: hội đồng phải xử lý nhiều công việc hơn và có ít thời gian thảo luận hơn . Đáp án đúng: How closer examination has affected firms ( Sự xem xét kỹ hơn đã tác động đến doanh nghiệp như thế nào ). Heading thứ 4. “ Thiếu giám đốc có kinh nghiệm đủ rộng ”: Chi tiết làm việc bán thời gian (“part-time”) ở câu (2) dễ khiến ta suy ra các giám đốc thiếu kinh nghiệm Nhưng đoạn nói về yêu cầu thời gian tăng, không phải tình trạng thiếu người có kinh nghiệm. Heading thứ 5. “ Một đề xuất thay đổi cách vận hành hội đồng quản trị ”: Câu (2) đặt nghi vấn (“throws doubt”) về mô hình hiện tại nên dễ tạo cảm giác đoạn sắp đề xuất thay đổi Nhưng đoạn chỉ mô tả áp lực và hệ quả, chưa đưa ra phương án thay thế.

The danger that some directors are left out of key decisions “ — Nguy cơ một số thành viên hội đồng bị đứng ngoài các quyết định quan trọng ”: Câu (4) cho thấy các thành viên bán thời gian không thể sánh về kiến thức (“could never match”) Nhưng thiếu thông tin không đồng nghĩa với bị loại khỏi quyết định; heading này cũng bỏ mất đề xuất trung tâm. Conflicts about the rewards given to top executives “ — Xung đột về thù lao dành cho lãnh đạo cấp cao ”: nếu chỉ bắt gặp vấn đề trả thù lao (“how to reward them”) ở câu (3). Nhưng đây chỉ là một câu hỏi khi triển khai mô hình mới, không phải một cuộc xung đột về thù lao.
explanation.step3: Bóc tách cấu trúc câu (S-V-O) và đối chiếu nghĩa.

questions.correct: Directors giving too little thought to the long term

explanation.step1: Đoạn E: A charge levelled again and again at boards is that too little of their attention goes to the long view — to strategy, to sustainability, to governance — while far too much is fixed on immediate profit . Both the rules they work under and the very shape of the market push them in this direction . The relentless rhythm of quarterly reporting can warp the choices a board reaches , since every four months its directors must 'hit the numbers' to feed a market forever hungry for fresh data . Such pressure rewards one particular breed of investor , the sort who slips in and out of a holding purely for a quick return and never troubles to discuss strategy or performance with the company . The tendency has sharpened as capital has gone global and as automated trading systems have come into ever wider use . Corporate culture bends to fit , and management , by and large, is paid to meet its commercial goals . Câu (1): nêu lời phê phán chính — ít chú ý đến dài hạn >< quá chú trọng lợi nhuận trước mắt. Câu (2)–(3): giải thích sức ép từ quy định, thị trường và báo cáo định kỳ khiến hội đồng chạy theo chỉ tiêu. Câu (4)–(5): sức ép ấy tạo lợi thế cho nhà đầu tư chuộng lợi nhanh; xu hướng này ngày càng mạnh. Câu (6): văn hóa doanh nghiệp và cơ chế trả công cũng điều chỉnh theo hướng đó. Đoạn E — too little of their attention
explanation.step2: Các giám đốc dành quá ít sự quan tâm cho dài hạn vì chịu sức ép chạy theo kết quả trước mắt. Đáp án đúng: Directors giving too little thought to the long term (Các giám đốc dành quá ít sự quan tâm cho dài hạn ). Đối chiếu paraphrasing: giving too little thought too little of their attention the long term the long view Conflicts about the rewards given to top executives “ (Xung đột về thù lao của lãnh đạo cấp cao) ”: nhầm vì câu (4) có từ thưởng hoặc tạo lợi thế (“rewards”), còn câu (6) nói được trả công (“is paid”). Nhưng đoạn không nêu xung đột về thù lao; các chi tiết này giải thích động lực chạy theo lợi ích trước mắt. Why every part of a business may have to be rethought “ (Vì sao mọi mặt của doanh nghiệp có thể cần được xem xét lại) ”: nhầm vì câu (6) nói văn hóa doanh nghiệp điều chỉnh để thích nghi (“bends to fit”). Nhưng đây là hệ quả của sức ép ngắn hạn, không phải lập luận rằng mọi mặt của doanh nghiệp cần được xem xét lại. How closer examination has affected firms “ (Việc xem xét kỹ hơn đã ảnh hưởng đến doanh nghiệp như thế nào) ”: Dễ đồng nhất báo cáo hằng quý (“quarterly reporting”) ở câu (3) với việc bị giám sát kỹ hơn Nhưng báo cáo ở đây được dùng để giải thích sức ép đạt chỉ tiêu trước mắt, tiếp nối lời phê phán về việc thiếu quan tâm dài hạn.
explanation.step3: Bóc tách cấu trúc câu (S-V-O) và đối chiếu nghĩa.
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: Directors giving too little thought to the long term

questions.correct: Conflicts about the rewards given to top executives

explanation.step1: Đoạn F: Pay for chief executives has turned into a battlefield on which investors, managers and board members wage set-piece struggles — sometimes out of sight , though more and more often under the bright lights of press coverage . To many observers that openness is precisely what transparency and sound governance demand , since shareholders bring their weight to bear on pay so as to force boards into dismissing chief executives who fail to deliver . Once such votes had been made legally binding , their capacity to strike down a company's pay policies grew stronger still . Chairing the remuneration committee can prove a lonely and badly exposed post , as Margery Thorne discovered at Kestrel Bank : she was obliged to step down after weathering a storm of criticism for defending a huge bonus destined for the chief executive — the irony being that , behind the committee's closed doors, she was widely believed to have argued against it . Câu (1): nêu chủ đề — xung đột về thù lao lãnh đạo , ngày càng công khai trên báo chí. Câu (2)–(3): triển khai sức ép của cổ đông; biểu quyết có ràng buộc pháp lý làm quyền bác bỏ chính sách thù lao mạnh hơn. Câu (4): minh họa bằng việc Thorne phải từ chức vì bảo vệ khoản thưởng , dù được cho là đã phản đối khoản thưởng đó. Đoạn F — Pay for chief executives
explanation.step2: Đoạn tập trung vào xung đột về lương, thưởng dành cho lãnh đạo cấp cao. Đáp án đúng: Conflicts about the rewards given to top executives (Những xung đột về thù lao dành cho lãnh đạo cấp cao ). Đối chiếu paraphrasing: Conflicts a battlefield the rewards given to top executives Pay for chief executives How closer examination has affected firms “ — Việc xem xét kỹ hơn đã ảnh hưởng đến các doanh nghiệp như thế nào ”: khi thấy báo chí đưa tin (“press coverage”) và Thorne chịu chỉ trích. Nhưng sự công khai chỉ là bối cảnh; trọng tâm xuyên suốt là tranh chấp về thù lao lãnh đạo, không phải ảnh hưởng của việc giám sát lên doanh nghiệp nói chung. The danger that some directors are left out of key decisions “ — Nguy cơ một số thành viên hội đồng bị gạt khỏi các quyết định quan trọng ”: khi thấy chuyện diễn ra sau cánh cửa đóng kín (“behind the committee's closed doors”). Nhưng Thorne được cho là đã phản đối khoản thưởng (“argued against it”), chứ không phải bị loại khỏi quá trình quyết định.
explanation.step3: Bóc tách cấu trúc câu (S-V-O) và đối chiếu nghĩa.

questions.correct: Why every part of a business may have to be rethought

explanation.step1: Đoạn G: Out of the financial crisis grew a broader conversation about what a company is actually for , together with a sharpened concern for corporate ethics . Faith in the corporation has worn thin , and thinkers such as Adrian Feld — whose bestseller The Limits of the Market has found a wide readership — now press hard questions about the morality of capitalism and of the market economy itself . In every sector , boards will have to broaden their outlook so as to take such matters in , and doing so may mean recasting the very goals a company sets for itself . These are demanding times . Câu (1)–(2): khủng hoảng khơi lên câu hỏi về mục đích và đạo đức doanh nghiệp, đi cùng sự suy giảm niềm tin và việc chất vấn nền kinh tế thị trường. Câu (3): từ đó, hội đồng ở mọi lĩnh vực phải mở rộng tầm nhìn, có thể tới mức định hình lại mục tiêu doanh nghiệp . Câu (4): kết lại bằng nhận định đây là giai đoạn đầy thách thức. Đoạn G — In every sector
explanation.step2: Niềm tin suy giảm và các chất vấn về đạo đức khiến doanh nghiệp có thể phải xem xét lại từ gốc , tới cả mục đích và mục tiêu hoạt động . Đáp án đúng: Why every part of a business may have to be rethought (Vì sao mọi mặt của doanh nghiệp có thể phải được xem xét lại ). Đối chiếu paraphrasing: Why Faith in the corporation has worn thin + corporate ethics may have to be rethought may mean recasting + the very goals How closer examination has affected firms “ (Tác động của việc giám sát kỹ hơn đối với doanh nghiệp) ”: Nếu chỉ thấy việc chất vấn (“press hard questions”) ở câu (2), dễ nhầm với giám sát doanh nghiệp kỹ hơn Nhưng trọng tâm là xem xét lại nền tảng và mục tiêu doanh nghiệp, không phải hệ quả của hoạt động giám sát. A suggestion for running the board differently “ (Một đề xuất thay đổi cách vận hành hội đồng quản trị) ”: Yêu cầu mở rộng tầm nhìn (“broaden their outlook”) dễ khiến ta nghĩ tới thay đổi cách vận hành hội đồng Nhưng câu (3) hướng tới mục tiêu doanh nghiệp, không đưa ra một mô hình tổ chức hội đồng cụ thể.
explanation.step3: Bóc tách cấu trúc câu (S-V-O) và đối chiếu nghĩa.
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: Why every part of a business may have to be rethought

questions.prompt: Boards generally make certain that every item on the agenda is given as much discussion time as it needs.

explanation.step1: Boards generally make certain that every item on the agenda is given as much discussion time as it needs . Ý câu hỏi: các hội đồng quản trị nhìn chung bảo đảm mỗi mục đều được thảo luận đủ thời gian theo nhu cầu .
explanation.step2: Câu hỏi không có từ khoá đặc biệt; ta đọc nhanh để tìm ý về chương trình họp và thời gian thảo luận. Ở đoạn B, cụm chương trình họp phình ra (“agendas swell”) cho biết đây là vùng liên quan. Đoạn B — agendas swell
explanation.step3: Đoạn B: When agendas swell in this way , the room left for genuine debate has to be squeezed so that the day's business can be got through .
explanation.step4: Câu hỏi nói: hội đồng quản trị bảo đảm mỗi mục được dành đủ thời gian thảo luận theo nhu cầu . Bài đọc nói: theo tác giả, khi chương trình họp phình ra, thời gian thảo luận thực chất phải bị thu hẹp (“ has to be squeezed ”) để xử lý hết công việc. Xử lý hết chương trình họp không đồng nghĩa với thảo luận đầy đủ . Quan điểm tác giả trái với nhận định. Đối chiếu paraphrasing: discussion time the room left for genuine debate as much discussion time as it needs has to be squeezed Đáp án đúng: NO Đáp án YES việc xử lý hết công việc (“the day's business can be got through”) với thảo luận đầy đủ. Nhưng tác giả nói thời gian thảo luận phải bị thu hẹp. Chỉ chọn YES nếu tác giả khẳng định mỗi mục vẫn được dành đủ thời gian thảo luận, kể cả khi chương trình họp phình ra. NOT GIVEN bài không nêu số phút cho từng mục. Nhưng tác giả đã trực tiếp nêu việc thời gian thảo luận bị thu hẹp; không cần số phút cụ thể để xác định sự trái ngược. Chỉ chọn NOT GIVEN nếu bài chỉ nói khối lượng công việc tăng mà không cho biết ảnh hưởng đến thời gian thảo luận.

questions.prompt: A committee's meeting can sometimes run on for longer than a meeting of the entire board.

explanation.step1: A committee's meeting can sometimes run on for longer than a meeting of the entire board . Ý câu hỏi: cuộc họp của một ủy ban đôi khi có thể kéo dài hơn cuộc họp của toàn bộ hội đồng quản trị; không khẳng định điều này luôn xảy ra.
explanation.step2: Câu hỏi không có từ khoá đặc biệt; ta đọc nhanh để tìm ý so sánh thời lượng hai cuộc họp. Ở đoạn C có từ mang nghĩa kéo dài hơn (“outlasts”) => đây là vùng liên quan. Đoạn C — outlasts
explanation.step3: Đoạn C: Indeed, a meeting of the audit committee not infrequently outlasts the gathering of the main board .
explanation.step4: Câu hỏi nói: cuộc họp ủy ban đôi khi có thể kéo dài hơn cuộc họp của toàn bộ hội đồng . Bài đọc nói: tác giả khẳng định cuộc họp ủy ban không hiếm khi (“not infrequently”) kéo dài hơn (“ outlasts ”) cuộc họp của toàn hội đồng . Không hiếm khi xảy ra thì chắc chắn có xảy ra trong một số trường hợp. Đối chiếu paraphrasing: A committee's meeting a meeting of the audit committee run on for longer than outlasts a meeting of the entire board the gathering of the main board Đáp án đúng: YES — nhận định trong câu hỏi phù hợp với quan điểm tác giả . Đáp án NO nếu đọc nhầm từ phủ định trong cụm không hiếm khi (“not infrequently”) thành không xảy ra. Nhưng tác giả đang xác nhận, không phủ nhận khả năng cuộc họp ủy ban kéo dài hơn. Chỉ chọn NO nếu tác giả nói cuộc họp ủy ban không bao giờ kéo dài hơn cuộc họp toàn hội đồng. NOT GIVEN bài không nêu số giờ hoặc số phút. Nhưng câu hỏi chỉ cần so sánh thời lượng, và từ kéo dài hơn (“outlasts”) đã cung cấp thông tin đó. Chỉ chọn NOT GIVEN nếu bài không cho biết cuộc họp nào có thể kéo dài hơn.

questions.prompt: Automated trading systems now account for the greater part of all share dealing.

explanation.step1: Automated trading systems now account for the greater part of all share dealing . Ý câu hỏi: tác giả có khẳng định hệ thống giao dịch tự động hiện chiếm phần lớn tổng giao dịch cổ phiếu hay không? Điểm cần kiểm tra là tỷ trọng chiếm đa số , không chỉ là mức sử dụng tăng.
explanation.step2: Dựa vào thuật ngữ chỉ hệ thống giao dịch tự động (“automated trading systems”) => ta bắt đầu đọc ở câu (5), đoạn E. Đoạn E — automated trading systems
explanation.step3: Đoạn E: The tendency has sharpened as capital has gone global and as automated trading systems have come into ever wider use .
explanation.step4: Câu hỏi nói: hệ thống giao dịch tự động hiện chiếm phần lớn tổng giao dịch cổ phiếu (“ the greater part of all share dealing ”). Bài đọc nói: các hệ thống này ngày càng được sử dụng rộng rãi (“have come into ever wider use ”), nhưng không cho biết tỷ trọng trong tổng giao dịch cổ phiếu . Tác giả không khẳng định cũng không phủ nhận tỷ trọng chiếm đa số . Được dùng rộng rãi hơn chưa đủ để kết luận chiếm phần lớn . Đối chiếu paraphrasing: ever wider use the greater part of all share dealing Đáp án đúng: NOT GIVEN Đáp án YES nhầm vì thấy mức sử dụng ngày càng rộng (“ever wider use”). Nhưng tăng mức sử dụng không đồng nghĩa với chiếm đa số. Chỉ chọn YES nếu tác giả xác nhận hệ thống tự động hiện chiếm phần lớn tổng giao dịch cổ phiếu. Đáp án NO Sai vì thiếu thông tin về tỷ trọng không có nghĩa là tác giả phủ nhận nhận định. Chỉ chọn NO nếu tác giả nói hệ thống tự động không chiếm phần lớn tổng giao dịch cổ phiếu.

questions.prompt: Shareholders became better able to reject executive pay policies once such votes were given legal force.

explanation.step1: Shareholders became better able to reject executive pay policies once such votes were given legal force . Ý câu hỏi: tác giả có cho rằng cổ đông có khả năng bác bỏ chính sách lương lãnh đạo tốt hơn sau khi việc bỏ phiếu có hiệu lực pháp lý hay không?
explanation.step2: Câu hỏi không có từ khoá đặc biệt; ta tìm ý cổ đông gây sức ép về lương. Đoạn F nhắc đến việc dùng ảnh hưởng để tác động đến lương (“bring their weight to bear on pay”) => đây là điểm bắt đầu đọc bằng chứng. Đoạn F — bring their weight to bear on pay
explanation.step3: Đoạn F: To many observers that openness is precisely what transparency and sound governance demand , since shareholders bring their weight to bear on pay so as to force boards into dismissing chief executives who fail to deliver . Once such votes had been made legally binding , their capacity to strike down a company's pay policies grew stronger still . Câu (2): xác định bối cảnh — cổ đông gây sức ép về lương của lãnh đạo điều hành. Câu (3): khi biểu quyết có tính ràng buộc pháp lý => khả năng bác bỏ chính sách lương tăng lên .
explanation.step4: Câu hỏi nói: cổ đông có khả năng bác bỏ tốt hơn sau khi việc bỏ phiếu có hiệu lực pháp lý. Bài đọc nói: tác giả khẳng định khả năng bác bỏ chính sách lương mạnh hơn (“ grew stronger ”) khi các cuộc bỏ phiếu trở nên ràng buộc về pháp lý (“ legally binding ”). Hai ý cùng chiều. Câu hỏi nói về khả năng , không đòi bằng chứng rằng cổ đông đã thực sự bác bỏ một chính sách cụ thể. Đối chiếu paraphrasing: became better able capacity + grew stronger reject strike down legal force legally binding Đáp án đúng: YES Đáp án NO Sai vì tác giả nói khả năng bác bỏ tăng lên, không phải giảm hoặc không cải thiện. Chỉ chọn NO nếu tác giả nói hiệu lực pháp lý không giúp cổ đông bác bỏ chính sách lương tốt hơn. NOT GIVEN Nếu đòi ví dụ về một chính sách đã thực sự bị bác bỏ, em dễ chọn NOT GIVEN Nhưng câu hỏi chỉ hỏi về khả năng, và câu (3) đã xác nhận khả năng ấy tăng lên. Chỉ chọn NOT GIVEN nếu tác giả chỉ nhắc hiệu lực pháp lý mà không cho biết khả năng bác bỏ có tăng hay không.

questions.prompt: Complete blank for Question 38:

explanation.step1: Ahead of the crash, the part-time non-executives were handicapped by having far less 12. ___ than the executives did. Ý câu hỏi: Trước cuộc khủng hoảng, nhóm không điều hành làm bán thời gian gặp bất lợi vì có ít hơn nhiều một thứ gì đó so với nhóm điều hành. Dự đoán ô trống: - Loại từ: danh từ không đếm được, đứng sau cụm chỉ lượng ít hơn nhiều (“far less”). - Loại thông tin: một thứ hoặc nguồn lực mà hai nhóm sở hữu ở mức độ khác nhau.
explanation.step2: Câu hỏi không có từ khoá đặc biệt; ta tìm ý so sánh giữa nhóm bán thời gian và nhóm điều hành. Ở đoạn D, cụm nói đồng nghiệp bán thời gian không thể sánh bằng (“their part-time colleagues could never match”) cho biết đây là vùng liên quan. Đoạn D — their part-time colleagues could never match
explanation.step3: Đoạn D: Even so, boards that were more professional and far better briefed would have served the banks especially well , for there the salaried executives commanded a depth of inside knowledge their part-time colleagues could never match — a gulf that left those non-executives unable to grasp or foresee the 2008 crash .
explanation.step4: Đáp án phù hợp nhất: knowledge Câu hoàn chỉnh: Ahead of the crash, the part-time non-executives were handicapped by having far less knowledge than the executives did. (Trước cuộc khủng hoảng, các thành viên không điều hành làm bán thời gian gặp bất lợi do có ít hiểu biết hơn nhiều so với các giám đốc điều hành.) => Khớp với dự đoán danh từ không đếm được: bài nói nhóm bán thời gian không thể sánh bằng mức hiểu biết của nhóm điều hành. Đáp án gồm 1 từ, lấy nguyên văn trong bài; đề được cung cấp không nêu giới hạn số từ. Đối chiếu paraphrasing: far less could never match were handicapped unable to grasp or foresee depth “ độ sâu ”: nằm ngay trong cụm “a depth of”. Nhưng từ này chỉ mức độ; thứ hai nhóm có mức độ chênh lệch là hiểu biết, không phải độ sâu nói chung. staff “ nhân sự hỗ trợ ”: Câu 1 đoạn D có nhắc đội ngũ hỗ trợ riêng (“dedicated staff”), nhưng đây là nguồn hỗ trợ cho mô hình hội đồng được đề xuất, không phải thứ được trực tiếp so sánh giữa hai nhóm trước cuộc khủng hoảng.

questions.prompt: Complete blank for Question 39:

explanation.step1: Directors give too much weight to 13. ___ that matters only in the near term . Ý câu hỏi: Các giám đốc coi trọng quá mức điều gì đó chỉ có ý nghĩa trong ngắn hạn . Dự đoán ô trống: - Loại từ: danh từ/cụm danh từ sau cấu trúc coi trọng (“give too much weight to”). Động từ “matters” gợi ý danh từ số ít hoặc không đếm được. - Nghĩa: một yếu tố được các giám đốc coi trọng quá mức, dù chỉ mang ý nghĩa ngắn hạn .
explanation.step2: Câu hỏi không có từ khoá đặc biệt; ta đọc nhanh để tìm ý các giám đốc chú trọng quá mức vào một yếu tố ngắn hạn. Ở đầu đoạn E, cụm tập trung quá nhiều vào (“far too much is fixed on”) cho biết nơi bắt đầu đọc. Đoạn E — far too much is fixed on
explanation.step3: Đoạn E: A charge levelled again and again at boards is that too little of their attention goes to the long view — to strategy, to sustainability, to governance — while far too much is fixed on immediate profit .
explanation.step4: Đáp án phù hợp nhất: profit Câu hoàn chỉnh: Directors give too much weight to profit that matters only in the near term . (Các giám đốc coi trọng quá mức lợi nhuận chỉ có ý nghĩa trong ngắn hạn .) => Khớp với dự đoán danh từ chỉ yếu tố được coi trọng quá mức: bài nói rõ đó là lợi nhuận trước mắt ; đáp án gồm 1 từ. Phần đề được cung cấp không nêu giới hạn từ. Đối chiếu paraphrasing: give too much weight to far too much is fixed on that matters only in the near term immediate strategy, sustainability, governance “ chiến lược, tính bền vững, quản trị ”: Nếu chỉ scan các danh từ gần đó, em dễ chọn nhầm nhóm này Nhưng chúng thuộc tầm nhìn dài hạn (“the long view”), phía được chú ý quá ít, trái với câu hỏi. attention “ sự chú ý ”: Từ này xuất hiện ngay trong câu bằng chứng, nhưng nó diễn tả sự chú ý được phân bổ, không phải thứ được coi trọng quá mức. immediate “ trước mắt ”: Sai vì đây là tính từ bổ nghĩa cho lợi nhuận, không thể đứng một mình ở vị trí danh từ cần điền. Ý thời gian này đã được câu hỏi diễn đạt bằng cụm ngắn hạn (“in the near term”).

questions.prompt: Complete blank for Question 40:

explanation.step1: The person heading the 14. ___ committee can find the role isolating and highly visible . Ý câu hỏi: Người đứng đầu một loại ủy ban có thể thấy vai trò này khiến mình cô lập và bị nhiều người chú ý. Dự đoán ô trống: - Loại từ: nhiều khả năng là danh từ bổ nghĩa cho danh từ ủy ban (“committee”). - Nghĩa cần tìm: loại ủy ban có người đứng đầu gặp tình trạng được mô tả.
explanation.step2: Câu hỏi không có từ khóa đặc biệt; ta đọc nhanh để tìm ý về người chủ trì ủy ban và một vai trò cô lập, bị nhiều người chú ý. Đoạn F có ý vị trí cô độc và bị soi xét nhiều (“a lonely and badly exposed post”) => đây là điểm bắt đầu đọc. Đoạn F — a lonely and badly exposed post
explanation.step3: Đoạn F: Chairing the remuneration committee can prove a lonely and badly exposed post , as Margery Thorne discovered at Kestrel Bank : she was obliged to step down after weathering a storm of criticism for defending a huge bonus destined for the chief executive — the irony being that, behind the committee's closed doors, she was widely believed to have argued against it .
explanation.step4: Đáp án phù hợp nhất: remuneration Câu hoàn chỉnh: The person heading the remuneration committee can find the role isolating and highly visible. (Người đứng đầu ủy ban thù lao có thể thấy vai trò này khiến mình cô lập và bị nhiều người chú ý.) => Khớp với dự đoán: danh từ xác định loại ủy ban, đồng thời gắn đúng với cả hai đặc điểm trong bài. Đáp án gồm 1 từ; đề được cung cấp không nêu giới hạn số từ. Đối chiếu paraphrasing: heading Chairing isolating lonely highly visible badly exposed audit “ — kiểm toán ”: nhầm vì đoạn C cũng nhắc đến ủy ban kiểm toán (“audit committee”). Nhưng thông tin đó nói về thời lượng họp, không mô tả vai trò cô lập và bị soi xét như câu (4). bonus “ — khoản thưởng ”: Từ này nằm trong phần minh họa của câu (4), nhưng chỉ khoản thưởng gây tranh cãi, không phải loại ủy ban. Đáp án pay “ — tiền lương ”: đoạn F bàn về tiền lương. Nhưng bài gọi chính xác ủy ban này là ủy ban thù lao (“remuneration committee”); không thay bằng một từ gần nghĩa.

content: 📌 Family Excursions

Lake cruise
Travel on an old steamship.
Passengers can photograph the [ _____ ] surrounding the lake.

Country Farm
Children may help feed the sheep.
The visit can include a forty-minute ride on a [ _____ ].
Visitors can walk through the farm’s [ _____ ] beside the lake.
[ _____ ] can be purchased for an additional charge.

Cycling trips
Cyclists follow the Back Road.
A [ _____ ] is supplied.
The route is suitable only for cyclists with some [ _____ ].
Bicycles can be rented from [ _____ ], near the Cruise Ship Terminal.
Cyclists need: 
- a repair kit
- food and drink 
- a [ _____ ], which can be hired
The area has no [ _____ ] or accommodation.

Cost
Total price for the family’s cruise and farm visit: $ [ _____ ].
transcript: [00:00] NARRATOR: You will hear a visitor asking a tourist centre employee about excursions for families. First, you have some time to look at questions one to four. Now listen carefully and answer questions one to four.
[00:51] TOURIST-CENTRE EMPLOYEE: Hello, what can I do for you?
[00:54] VISITOR: I'm trying to find out whether you offer any trips that would work for a family.
[00:59] TOURIST-CENTRE EMPLOYEE: Certainly. One possibility is a lake cruise. An old steamship, more than a century old, carries passengers several times each day.
[01:10] VISITOR: That sounds appealing. How long does the cruise last?
[01:15] TOURIST-CENTRE EMPLOYEE: Roughly an hour and a half. Make sure you bring a camera for the mountains. They rise all around the lake, and the view from the boat is excellent.
[01:26] VISITOR: Great. Is there somewhere on board to buy a drink or something to eat?
[01:31] TOURIST-CENTRE EMPLOYEE: Yes. How old are your children?
[01:34] VISITOR: My daughter's fifteen and my son is seven.

[01:38] TOURIST-CENTRE EMPLOYEE: In that case, you could turn the crossing into a full day out. A very popular option after you reach the other side is the country farm. The farmer meets visitors at the boat and takes them to the pens where the sheep are kept. Children can help feed them.
[01:56] VISITOR: My son would really enjoy that. He loves animals.
[02:01] TOURIST-CENTRE EMPLOYEE: There's also a forty minute trip around the farm on a horse if he'd like to try it.
[02:07] VISITOR: Would he cope with that? He's never ridden before.
[02:11] TOURIST-CENTRE EMPLOYEE: He should be fine. It's designed for complete beginners.
[02:16] VISITOR: Good.

[02:18] TOURIST-CENTRE EMPLOYEE: Visitors may also explore the farm independently, provided they shut the gates behind them. The farm owns some lovely gardens beside the lake, and they should look especially good at this time of year. You could easily spend an hour or two walking through them.
[02:36] VISITOR: That all sounds ideal. Can we have lunch there as well?
[02:41] TOURIST-CENTRE EMPLOYEE: Yes, and the food is very good. Lunch isn't covered by the standard price though, so you pay for it at the farm.
[02:49] VISITOR: Understood.
[02:53] NARRATOR: Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions five to ten. Now listen and answer questions five to ten.
[03:41] VISITOR: Is there anything else we could do on that side of the lake?

[03:45] TOURIST-CENTRE EMPLOYEE: You could take bicycles across on the ship and follow a cycling route called the back road. It takes about three or four hours to explore, and the scenery is beautiful. When you collect your cruise ticket, they give you a map at no additional charge.
[04:02] VISITOR: How difficult is the route?
[04:05] TOURIST-CENTRE EMPLOYEE: Some stretches are quite demanding, so it wouldn't be appropriate for your seven-year-old. Cyclists need to have some experience.
[04:14] VISITOR: My daughter and I both enjoy cycling, so perhaps we could do that while my wife and son remain at the farm. But we haven't brought bicycles. Is there anywhere nearby that hires them?
[04:26] TOURIST-CENTRE EMPLOYEE: Yes, there's a shop in the city called Ratchesons.
[04:29] VISITOR: Let me write that down. How is it spelled?
[04:33] TOURIST-CENTRE EMPLOYEE: R-A-T-C-H-E-S-O-N-S. It's just by the cruise ship terminal.
[04:41] VISITOR: Thanks.
[04:42] TOURIST-CENTRE EMPLOYEE: You should collect a repair kit there as well. You'll also need a snack and some water, and it's best to buy those in the city before you leave.
[04:52] VISITOR: No problem. I can hire a helmet at the bicycle shop too, can't I?

[04:58] TOURIST-CENTRE EMPLOYEE: Yes, and you should definitely take one. It's a wonderful ride, but the route is isolated. There aren't any shops or places to stay in that area, so you must return in time for the final boat.
[05:13] VISITOR: Right. What would the whole day cost us?

[05:16] TOURIST-CENTRE EMPLOYEE: Let me calculate it. One adult and one child taking the cruise and farm visit comes to $117, while the cruise only tickets for another adult and child bring the total to $214. Actually, how old did you say your daughter was?
[05:38] VISITOR: Fifteen.
[05:39] TOURIST-CENTRE EMPLOYEE: Then the total is $267, I'm afraid. She has to pay the adult fare of $75, rather than the child fare of $22. Sorry about that.
[05:54] VISITOR: That's all right. So how to...
[05:59] NARRATOR: That is the end of part one.

passages.title: Talk To New Kitchen Assistants
content: 🎧 HƯỚNG DẪN NGHE PART 2: "Talk To New Kitchen Assistants"

Bấm nút Play trên trình phát Audio phía trên để nghe bài thu âm chuẩn quốc tế và hoàn thành các câu hỏi ở cột bên phải. Bạn có thể chuyển sang tab "Transcript Hội Thoại" để đối chiếu lời thoại chi tiết và bấm giờ từng câu.
transcript: [00:00] AUDIO: You will hear a restaurant manager speaking to a group of new kitchen assistants. First you have some time to look at questions 11 to 16. Now listen carefully and answer questions 11 to 16. Good morning, everyone.

[00:52] AUDIO: I'm Joy Parkins, the restaurant manager. I gather that none of you has worked as a kitchen assistant before. You may be a little anxious, but most assistants tell us they enjoy the job. Occasionally someone may speak sharply to you, but it isn't personal.

[01:09] AUDIO: What people particularly like is the variety. There are so many different tasks that the work never becomes dull. And if you perform well, there may be opportunities to move up and take on greater responsibility. You've all arrived punctually, which is an excellent beginning.

[01:31] AUDIO: I'm also pleased that everyone is wearing suitable shoes because kitchen floors can become wet and slippery. Those with long hair have tied it back properly. However, a few of you are still wearing rings or bracelets. Please put that jewelry somewhere secure today and leave it at home from tomorrow as it can create a safety risk.

[01:52] AUDIO: Today will be extremely busy. There are no tables available for dinner, and only a small number remain for lunch. Luckily, our head chef has returned. He was on holiday throughout last week, so the other chefs had to take on additional work.

[02:10] AUDIO: Before I explain the job in more detail, I need to cover some general rules. Regardless of age, nobody may operate certain equipment until they have received the appropriate training. The waste disposal unit is one example. I believe two of you, Emma and Jake, are under 18.

[02:32] AUDIO: That means the meat slicer is completely off-limits to you, and none of you may use the electric mixer until someone has demonstrated it. You may have heard that kitchen work can be stressful, and sometimes it is. During your first week, each shift will last eight hours. After that, you can volunteer for overtime if you wish.

[02:55] AUDIO: Whatever hours you work, you will still have a break halfway through. The physically difficult part is spending the whole day standing, lifting, and carrying, so you'll soon become fitter if you aren't already. There's rarely an opportunity to slow down. When a chef gives an instruction, you must act on it immediately.

[03:18] AUDIO: On the positive side, our air conditioning system is much better than the systems in many kitchens. Before you hear the rest of the talk, you have some time to look at questions 17 to 20. Now listen and answer questions 17 to 20. I'll now introduce some members of staff you need to know.

[04:19] AUDIO: As I mentioned, I'm Joy Parkins. I arrange what each person does during the day and decide how long everyone works. I'll rotate you among different colleagues in the kitchen so that you can learn while doing the job. Another important name is David Field.

[04:37] AUDIO: If you hurt yourself even slightly, report it to him. He'll record what happened and make sure you receive the right treatment. He is qualified to provide basic first aid himself, or he'll send you elsewhere if more help is needed. Then there's Dexter Wills.

[04:56] AUDIO: Speak to him whenever you break a plate or any other item. Don't leave it and hope the damage goes unnoticed. Breakages must be recorded and replacements arranged, otherwise difficulties may arise later. Finally, Mike Smith manages our supplies of perishable food.
[05:16] AUDIO: If you see that flour, sugar, or anything similar is running low, tell him so he can order more. All right, the next thing. That is the end of part two.

content: Study of local library: possible areas to investigate

transcript: [00:00] NARRATOR: You will hear two students, Trudy and Stewart, planning a paper about public libraries. First, you have some time to look at questions 21 to 23. Now listen carefully and answer questions 21 to 23.
[00:54] TRUDIE: Right, Stewart, we need to begin planning our paper on public libraries. Have you decided what approach we might take?
[01:02] STEWART: There are so many possibilities. We could examine the way libraries have developed through history or compare how they're run in different countries. What would you prefer?

[01:16] TRUDIE: Perhaps we should limit the study to this country and connect developments in libraries with wider social changes. For example, literacy is much more widespread than it was a hundred years ago and a local community may now use many different languages.
[01:36] STEWART: We might also mention how their sources of finance have altered.
[01:41] TRUDIE: We could, but the assignment is only a short paper, so I don't think funding should be covered in detail.
[01:48] STEWART: Fair enough. Shall we generate a few ideas first?

[01:54] TRUDIE: Yes. We clearly have to discuss the effect of new technology, especially the internet. Because so many books have been converted into digital form, readers can reach them from their computers at home.
[02:09] STEWART: If everybody chose that option, libraries might become unnecessary.
[02:15] TRUDIE: True.

[02:16] STEWART: But most digital books that can be read online without payment are no longer protected by copyright, aren't they? Here, copyright continues for 70 years after an author's death. That means recent bestsellers and current information generally aren't available free.
[02:36] TRUDIE: That's worth including. Personally, I struggle to focus on a long piece of writing on a screen. I'd rather use a printed book, and reading from a screen takes me longer.
[02:49] STEWART: I actually prefer the screen, so perhaps that's simply down to individual taste.

[02:56] TRUDIE: Probably. Libraries are likely to keep changing over the coming years. Some already provide venues for community activities, such as meetings of local clubs. And I imagine that role will expand.

[03:10] STEWART: I hope so, and I'd like them to preserve their established purpose too, but I'm doubtful. Cost will influence what happens. My concern is that printed books and magazines will vanish entirely, and libraries will contain nothing except rows of computers. They'd be completely unlike the places we know now.
[03:33] TRUDIE: We'll have to wait and see.
[03:38] NARRATOR: Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions 24 to 30. Now listen, and answer questions 24 to 30.
[04:24] TRUDIE: I've just thought of something. We could carry out a detailed study of our local public library to provide background for the paper.

[04:33] STEWART: That would be interesting and would give us plenty of issues to investigate. Let's list possible questions and then arrange them into a structure. We could interview staff, for instance, and ask whether the library controls its own budget or whether the local council manages it.

[04:53] TRUDIE: We should also ask about their policies. I know eating isn't permitted, but I'd like to discover which kinds of noise are prohibited. People often talk there, whereas you never hear music. I don't know whether that results from an official rule or just happens naturally.
[05:14] STEWART: I've wondered about that too. We could then consider how employment law affects the library. There must be regulations covering staff hours, workplace facilities and similar matters.

[05:29] TRUDIE: Yes. Other questions concern the building's design and the way visitors use it. What does the library do to protect customers' safety? Non-slip flooring and emergency exits would be examples.
[05:45] TRUDIE: We should also find out what insurance it must hold in case somebody is injured.
[05:50] STEWART: Good point. There's something else I've often wanted to understand.
[05:56] TRUDIE: What is it?

[05:57] STEWART: You know, the library keeps an archive of local newspapers stretching back many years. Beside it is the diary of a prominent politician from the late 19th century. Why is it stored there? Do you know how he was linked to the area?

[06:15] TRUDIE: I don't. Let's include that in our questions. And local people may ask the library for information about organisations such as sports clubs. I wonder whether the staff maintain a database or simply search online.
[06:32] STEWART: Yes. I'd also like to explore how a public library differs from one located inside a museum. They must operate in quite different ways.
[06:44] TRUDIE: Mmm. Another thing I'd be interested to learn is...
[06:51] NARRATOR: That is the end of part three.

passages.title: Four Business Values
content: 📌 Four business values

The use of many business values can cause [ _____ ].
Senior leaders must recognise and manage the possible [ _____ ] that can follow.

Collaboration
As part of a training course, the speaker’s group had to build a [ _____ ].
Attempts by the other groups to work collaboratively resulted in [ _____ ].
The speaker’s group succeeded by limiting collaboration.
Collaboration contributed to weak sales of a [ _____ ].

Industriousness
Poorly directed effort can waste important company [ _____ ].
In this model, “lazy” describes people who choose not to carry out [ _____ ] tasks.

Creativity
A memorable campaign for a [ _____ ] did not increase sales.
Creative activity should focus on a specific [ _____ ].

Excellence
One study found that pioneers achieved an average [ _____ ] far above that of followers.
Businesses that always pursue excellence can lose opportunities.
transcript: [00:00] AUDIO: You will hear a lecturer discussing four values commonly associated with business. First, you have some time to look at questions 31 to 40. Now listen carefully and answer questions 31 to 40. When people discuss business, they often assume that certain values are unquestionably desirable.

[01:01] AUDIO: Today I'll consider four of them – collaboration, industriousness, creativity and excellence. Most of us would describe all four as positive, but I want to argue that the reality is less simple. The difficulty is that these values are abstract ideas and can become detached from what happens in a company from day to day. Organisations can certainly pursue them, but they must anticipate the consequences.

[01:35] AUDIO: Although nobody intends it, applying these values may actually cause damage. Senior managers normally want to make sound decisions. Yet the apparent right choice can produce the opposite result when leaders adopt a value without recognising and controlling its side effects. In practice, the value may obstruct the very objective it was meant to support.

[02:01] AUDIO: Let's begin with collaboration. I once attended a management course where participants were divided into teams and asked to construct a bridge over a stream using a set of building blocks. One rule required every team member to move at least one block during construction, supposedly to promote teamwork. In fact, one person could perform the task far more effectively.

[02:30] AUDIO: The other groups tried to make every decision together and quickly fell into confusion, with people obstructing one another. Our leader handled the challenge cleverly. She had each member shift a block a few centimetres to satisfy the rule, then allowed the person who was best at puzzles to finish the structure alone. We completed it first.

[02:58] AUDIO: The lesson is that the task did not suit collaboration, so imposing teamwork made little sense. Collaboration can also produce an inconsistent product, which often damages sales. One company launched a smartphone while two directors pursued conflicting markets. One wanted business customers.

[03:23] AUDIO: The other insisted on ordinary consumers. To involve them both, the company selected a consumer-style name but promoted the phone to businesses. It appealed fully to neither group. Allowing either director to follow a single strategy would have been more effective.

[03:46] AUDIO: The second value is industriousness, or hard work. It's easy to joke about people who emphasise how hard they work. A hamster runs continuously in its wheel, but never advances. Effort is valuable only when directed well.

[04:05] AUDIO: Otherwise, it consumes the company resources that matter most, time and energy, without benefiting the organisation. One management model places people into categories using four qualities – clever, hard-working, stupid and lazy. In this model, being lazy means making a rational choice not to perform unnecessary tasks. It does not mean refusing to work.

[04:38] AUDIO: Most people combine two qualities, and the most useful employees are both clever and lazy. They think clearly and avoid rushing into decisions. Instead of adding more working hours to a problem, they seek a solution that saves the time and energy wasted by people who work hard without thinking effectively. We now turn to creativity.

[05:06] AUDIO: It can be productive. An inventive television advertisement may attract attention and increase sales. But originality does not always deliver a commercial result. Some campaigns remain in people's memories while doing nothing for the product.

[05:25] AUDIO: This occurred during the launch of a chocolate bar. Later research found that many consumers remembered the advertisements but could not identify what had been advertised. The creator enjoyed developing the concept and wrongly assumed the audience would respond in the same way. A business that releases thousands of products may appear more creative than one producing only a handful, yet excessive creativity can reduce profits.

[06:00] AUDIO: Creative work should be directed towards solving a specific problem the company has identified. Producing an endless stream of novel items is not automatically useful. The final value is excellence. Many companies claim that they pursue it, but achieving excellence takes time.

[06:21] AUDIO: In business, introducing the first version of a product can be more profitable than offering the finest version. A major performance study compared pioneers, the firms that launched a product first, with followers that copied and improved it. On average, pioneers secured a market share of 29%, while followers achieved just 13%, less than half as much even when the later product was superior. Requiring excellence in every activity consumes time and energy and may cause a company to miss opportunities.

[07:03] AUDIO: Work that is merely adequate can sometimes be more valuable than perfect work. Telling people to make everything excellent may sound sensible, but beginning promptly is often the more successful approach.

[00:51] MAN: Good morning, Kenton festival box office. How may I help?
[00:56] WOMAN: Hello, I'm spending a few days in Kenton next month and a friend mentioned that a festival would be taking place. She gave me this number so I could ask for details.
[01:09] MAN: Yes, the festival starts on the 16th of May and continues until the 19th.
[01:15] WOMAN: Perfect. I'll be there from the 15th to the 19th. Could you tell me what's included in the program?

[01:23] MAN: Certainly. On the opening day, there's a ceremony in the town center. People generally begin arriving at about two o'clock so they can find a good viewing place. The program itself begins at 2 45 and should finish at around 5 30.
[01:41] WOMAN: Thanks. I'll arrive early enough to get a good position.
[01:46] MAN: The mayor will formally open the festival with a short welcome. All the town counselors will attend, along with many local residents.
[01:54] WOMAN: Right.
[01:56] MAN: After the mayor's speech, a band will perform. We usually invite a children's choir, but this year the local army cadets volunteered and they're excellent.
[02:07] WOMAN: I see.
[02:08] MAN: Next, a community group from Kenton will present a short play they've written. It's about Helen Tungate. Have you heard of her?
[02:19] WOMAN: Yes, of course. She was a scientist.
[02:23] MAN: Exactly. She was born in Kenton 100 years ago. So the town is marking the centenary of her birth.
[02:32] WOMAN: I'm a biologist, so I've always found her work interesting. I hadn't realized she was from Kenton.

[02:40] MAN: All those activities take place during the afternoon. Later around sunset, there'll be a fireworks display. The park is the best place to watch because the fireworks are set off from the opposite bank of the river. It's consistently one of the festival's most popular attractions.
[02:59] WOMAN: That sounds wonderful.
[03:04] NARRATOR: Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions 6 to 10. Now listen and answer questions 6 to 10.
[03:51] WOMAN: What events are planned for the remaining days?
[03:55] MAN: Several run throughout the festival. The art college students, for example, have made a series of videos exploring relationships between children and their grandparents.
[04:09] WOMAN: That sounds unusual. We hear far more about children and their parents.
[04:14] MAN: That's true. The art college is still being used for lessons during the festival, so the videos will be screened at Handsworth House.
[04:23] WOMAN: Could you spell that for me?
[04:27] MAN: Certainly. H-A-N-D-S-W-O-R-T-H. Handsworth House is near the town hall.
[04:41] WOMAN: Got it.
[04:42] MAN: Let me see what else might interest you.
[04:45] WOMAN: Will there be any ballet performances? I do ballet as a hobby, so I'd particularly like to see one.
[04:53] MAN: I'm afraid ballet isn't on the program. However, there will be a demonstration of traditional dances from different parts of the country.
[05:04] WOMAN: That would be enjoyable. Where will it take place?
[05:08] MAN: In the town center market, the outdoor market, rather than the covered one. Performances are at 2 and 5 each afternoon, except on the festival's first day.
[05:21] WOMAN: Lovely. I enjoy every kind of dance, so I'm sure I'll like it.
[05:28] MAN: I expect you will.
[05:29] WOMAN: I'd also like to attend a concert, if any are being held.
[05:33] MAN: There are four. Three given by professional musicians and one performed by local children.
[05:40] WOMAN: Where will those be?
[05:42] MAN: At the library in Part Street. The children's concert is at 6.30 in the evening on the 18th.
[05:50] WOMAN: I assume I'll need a ticket.
[05:53] MAN: Yes. You can reserve one online, purchase it at the festival box office after you arrive, or buy it from any shop displaying the festival logo in its window.

[06:12] MAN: You're welcome. I hope you have a wonderful stay.

content: 🎧 HƯỚNG DẪN NGHE PART 2: "Theatre Trip To Munich"

Bấm nút Play trên trình phát Audio phía trên để nghe bài thu âm chuẩn quốc tế và hoàn thành các câu hỏi ở cột bên phải. Bạn có thể chuyển sang tab "Transcript Hội Thoại" để đối chiếu lời thoại chi tiết và bấm giờ từng câu.
transcript: [00:00] AUDIO: You will hear a man giving a group updated information about a theater trip to Munich. First, you have some time to look at questions 11 to 15. Now listen carefully and answer questions 11 to 15. Right, I've nearly finished arranging our tour, so I can now update you on the details that have been confirmed.

[01:01] AUDIO: As you know, we fly to Munich first. On Monday the 4th, our flight leaves at 11.30, which is too early for lunch at the airport. I suggest that we meet there at 10 for coffee. That should still leave everyone enough time to eat breakfast before leaving home.

[01:24] AUDIO: At Munich Airport, Klaus Bauer will be waiting for us. Klaus is employed by a tour operator, and he'll take care of the group throughout our time in Germany. He has already contacted the managers of all the theaters we'll visit. He has also arranged for a staff member from Munich's national theater to give us a tour of the building one afternoon.

[01:52] AUDIO: When we last discussed the trip, I couldn't give you the exact hotel price, but that has now been settled. The standard charge for a double room is 150 euros per night. I'd hoped to reduce it to 120, but I've actually negotiated a price of 110 euros. This reduction will be included in the final amount you must pay by the end of this week.

[02:23] AUDIO: On Tuesday, our first full day, I'd planned for us to observe a theater rehearsal. Unfortunately, that has been impossible to organize. Instead, a coach will take us to visit one of the remarkable castles in the mountains south of Munich. We'll all eat together on Tuesday evening at a restaurant close to the hotel.

[02:49] AUDIO: After asking about everyone's preferences, I realized that a typical regional restaurant would serve too much meat for some members of the group. Several of you proposed an Italian place. However, I eventually reserved a Lebanese restaurant because we have plenty of chances to eat Italian food at home. On Wednesday afternoon, we'll meet the director of the play we're attending that evening.

[03:19] AUDIO: She'll explain the complete production process, including her selection of the actors, and, because it is a modern play, the way she collaborated with the playwright. Before you hear the rest of the talk, you have some time to look at questions 16 to 20. Now listen and answer questions 16 to 20. I'd now like to explain a few things about the plays on our schedule.

[04:26] AUDIO: The information may affect which clothes you decide to pack. Wednesday evening's production is contemporary, and we'll be attending its premiere, so the occasion will be fairly elegant, although formal dress isn't required. It's apparently a multimedia production, with striking lighting and a recorded electronic soundtrack. Unfortunately, the playwright is unwell, and probably won't be there.

[04:58] AUDIO: Thursday's play originally opened last year. The town commissioned it to commemorate the 100th anniversary of the birth of a famous local scientist. We'll see a revival of that well-received production. Friday's event makes clothing more difficult to plan, because the performance takes place in the garden of a palace.

[05:24] AUDIO: The surroundings are beautiful, but there'll be very little shelter if the weather is windy. On Saturday, a coach will take us to a theater in a nearby town. The performance opens a drama festival, and the mayor and the town's other officials will all attend. Afterwards, the mayor will hold a reception for the entire audience, with a band performing traditional music from the region.

[05:55] AUDIO: Sunday is a free day. Our final play is on Monday, inside the old town hall, a magnificent building dating from the 14th century. The occasion celebrates the leading actor's 50 years on the stage, and this is the play in which he made his first professional appearance. We fly home the following day.
[06:22] AUDIO: Now, does anyone have a question before I? That is the end of part two.

passages.title: Scandinavian Studies
content: 📌 How James will prepare his paper on the Vikings
transcript: [00:00] NARRATOR: You will hear a tutor, Beth, meeting James for his first Scandinavian studies tutorial. First, you have some time to look at questions 21 to 25. Now listen carefully and answer questions 21 to 25.
[00:52] BETH: Good morning. You must be James. I'm Beth Cartwright, but please call me Beth.
[00:59] JAMES: Thank you.
[01:00] BETH: Since this is your first tutorial after beginning the Scandinavian studies course, I'd like to learn little about you. What made you choose the subject?

[01:11] JAMES: My mother is Danish. Although our family always lived in England, she spoke frequently about Denmark, which made me want to go there. We rarely visited together because she usually travelled by herself. However, whenever her relatives or Danish friends came to England, they always stayed with or visited our family.
[01:34] BETH: I see. So you can already speak some Danish, one of the languages on the course.
[01:41] JAMES: I can manage an everyday conversation, although I make quite a few mistakes.
[01:46] BETH: You'll probably know that the third year is spent overseas. Have you considered where you'd like to go?
[01:53] JAMES: I'm really looking forward to that year. Denmark would be the obvious choice because of my family, but I'd love to spend it in Iceland.
[02:02] BETH: I'm sure that can be arranged. What are your plans after graduation? Many students continue to a master's degree.

[02:11] JAMES: Four years of undergraduate study will probably be enough for me. Journalism interests me, and I like the idea of living in Scandinavia and writing for magazines. That seems more creative than working as a translator, which is what many graduates apparently do.
[02:32] BETH: All right. How are you getting on with this term's courses?
[02:37] JAMES: I'm particularly enjoying Swedish cinema.

[02:39] BETH: That course carries on next term. The present Scandinavian literature course, however, finishes this term and will be replaced by more specialised options. And, if Danish television appeals to you, a course about it will begin the term after next.
[02:59] JAMES: That sounds interesting.
[03:01] BETH: Have you considered a subject for the literature paper due in the next few weeks?
[03:07] JAMES: My first choice would be the Icelandic sagas.
[03:10] BETH: The difficulty is that many students select that subject so the books you need can be hard to obtain. It might be better to save it for a later assignment.
[03:21] JAMES: All right.
[03:22] BETH: You could look at modern novels or 19th century playwrights instead.
[03:27] JAMES: I've read several translated plays and seen some performed, so playwrights would suit me.
[03:33] BETH: Good. I'll record that as your topic.
[03:37] JAMES: What kind of approach would you recommend?

[03:39] BETH: To begin with, don't concentrate in great depth on just one author. That can be valuable later, but first you need to understand the literature within the society that produced it, its intended readers, the way it was published, and related issues. That would be more useful at this stage than simply tracing the genre's history.
[04:05] JAMES: That makes sense.
[04:09] NARRATOR: Before you hear the rest of the tutorial, you have some time to look at questions 26 to 30. Now listen and answer questions 26 to 30.
[04:57] JAMES: Could you also advise me about the Vikings paper I have to complete this week? I'm not sure how to begin.
[05:04] BETH: Of course. Have you selected a topic?
[05:07] JAMES: Not yet. There are too many interesting possibilities. Viking settlements abroad, trade, mythology, and so on.

[05:16] BETH: Start by reading a student paper from last year that is kept in the library. It's brief and tightly focused, so it should help you choose. A textbook usually covers such a wide range that it can make selecting one subject even harder.
[05:33] JAMES: I have a DVD of the Viking film released earlier this year. Would it help if I watched it again?

[05:39] BETH: If it's the film I'm thinking of, I'd leave it alone. It contains more fantasy than fact. I can lend you a recording of a documentary instead. It raises some challenging points that should help you narrow the topic.
[05:54] JAMES: Good. Once I've done that, should I create an outline?

[05:59] BETH: Yes. At first, just decide on headings for the different sections so that you establish the structure. Then find suitable articles and books, take notes from them, and organise those notes beneath the relevant headings.
[06:16] JAMES: I understand.
[06:18] BETH: Next, add short phrases and sentences as bullet points under each heading. Check that this framework is logical and flows clearly before you write the complete paper.
[06:31] JAMES: Thank you. That's extremely helpful.

content: 📌 Conflict At Work

Much workplace conflict belongs to the broad category of [ _____ ].
It frequently results from a desire to display [ _____ ].
Conflict may also arise because people have different [ _____ ].
“[ _____ ]” conflicts occur when employees prioritise their own group over the whole company.
Stress caused by conflict may cause prolonged [ _____ ] from work.

Chief executives
Many CEOs experience both [ _____ ] and anxiety.
They may not respond well when others question their choices.
Conflict may occur between people with different [ _____ ].

Other managers
A more [ _____ ] organisational structure can make reporting relationships unclear.

Reducing conflict
Managers must make a sustained effort to gain employees’ [ _____ ].
An independent outsider may play a role as a [ _____ ] to help resolve a dispute.
transcript: [00:00] AUDIO: You will hear a lecturer discussing the causes and management of conflict in the workplace. First, you have some time to look at questions 31 to 40. Now listen carefully and answer questions 31 to 40. Conflicts are now much better, conflict remains common in organizations, and modern human resources managers must know how to handle it.

[01:14] AUDIO: So what counts as workplace conflict? Definitions differ, but I use the term for a broad range of conduct that a victim considers unacceptable. It can extend from relatively minor, harmless disputes to physical violence. A large proportion falls under the general heading of bullying.

[01:36] AUDIO: By that, I mean one or more people acting aggressively or abusively toward somebody in a weaker position. Every instance of bullying is conflict, although workplace conflict is not always bullying. As with other forms of human behavior, there are many possible causes. Frequently, a person wants to demonstrate superiority over somebody else because doing so reassures them that they are not at the bottom of a social or organizational hierarchy.

[02:10] AUDIO: Sometimes, two individuals simply dislike each other because their personalities are incompatible. An employee who is habitually optimistic, for example, may have little patience with a colleague who is continually pessimistic. Naturally, that still doesn't excuse poor treatment. A further type develops when employees care more about advancing themselves and their own team than about the organization as a whole.

[02:40] AUDIO: These are known as structural conflicts. They might occur when a sales department believes it alone contributes useful work and consequently looks down on administrative staff who operate behind the scenes. Conflict clearly harms the people involved. Victims may experience severe stress, leading to an absence from work that can continue for several months.

[03:06] AUDIO: If the company makes no attempt to intervene, the dispute may grow uncontrollably and, in an extreme case, contribute to the organization's collapse. Research involving chief executives, or CEOs, has revealed why some treat colleagues badly. Many display two, apparently opposite, characteristics. Strong confidence in their capacity to achieve important results, together with considerable anxiety about failing to meet targets set by themselves or by company directors.

[03:46] AUDIO: This combination may cause them to react badly when anyone challenges a decision. In a high-pressure workplace, those characteristics create particular difficulties. The problem becomes more serious when colleagues, managers, and board members each pursue different visions. If they cannot agree on strategy or on the future direction of the business, substantial conflict follows.

[04:15] AUDIO: Lower-level managers might assume that an autocratic organization, in which the CEO issues instructions and everybody else obeys, generates the most conflict. Interestingly, a more democratic structure may experience greater difficulties. Uncertainty about whom employees report to can result in contradictory demands. Let's now consider how damaging conflict can be reduced.

[04:46] AUDIO: Preventing it from arising is obviously the ideal. A capable manager at any level will work to earn the respect of colleagues, especially direct reports. This means communicating politely and treating employees as equals whose organizational roles happen to differ. Conflict does sometimes occur and may become unmanageable.

[05:12] AUDIO: Human resources will often intervene. However, one party may view that department merely as the chief executive's spokesperson. In that situation, an independent person from outside the organization can act as a mediator. By speaking with both sides, establishing what occurred, and presenting an impartial account, this person may offer feedback that each party accepts precisely because it comes from outside the company.
